findings.finding: The telescoping and star-generator identities hold in arbitrary groups. All endpoint-indexed subgroups, including reversed and empty pairs, are accounted for.

Finite generation as a monoid makes Cayley propagation exhaustive. A successful bijection preserves products, not merely generator edges. For flag maps, connectivity fixes the parity choice and color0 forces the same map on both copies.
Hereditary intersection tests and strict subgroup growth establish complete search in every possible finite rank. Generation cannot occur at a proper prefix of a valid final tuple.

The classical reflection criterion is transported with Aut(G), not inner automorphisms. It is involutory because its square fixes all generators; the first entry of order>2 prevents it being identity.
The Schulte–Weiss geometry/stabilizer theorem is explicit retained input. The application does not assert arbitrary string relations suffice, or claim the general non-string hypertope theorem.

The right-action derivation of G×{+,-} agrees after the declared parity swap. Ordinary colored flag isomorphisms preserve the reconstructed poset and conversely. This validates the mirror correction as an unrooted convention statement.

Odd special-linear involutions are complementary line/plane decompositions; even ones have rank-one square-zero nilpotent part. Unitary norm counts, rank-one form preservation, and odd central kernels yield the stated counts, including q2 and nonsimple small groups.
Liebeck–Shalev remains an attributed bound. No numerical constant or timing speedup is deduced from its asymptotic form.
The native independent rotation search and literal A5 involution check confirm the correction witnesses. The universal arbitrary-group claims are the written proof, not these tests.
